S08.meta: // SLIDE 08 — THE ASYMMETRY: POSITIVE VS NEGATIVE BIOPSY

data.question: The biopsy is negative — is the lesion benign?

branches.label: Positive biopsy
branches.detail: Malignant cells identified — they were present in the sample. Highly reliable.

branches.label: Negative biopsy
branches.detail: No malignancy in this sample — consistent with no cancer, or with a cancer the needle did not reach
branches.fix: Assess whether the needle sampled the right tissue before accepting result

resolver.label: The failure is silent
resolver.detail: The report says what was in the sample. It does not say whether the sample was the right tissue. Reliability of a negative result is bounded by confidence the needle was in the right place.

S09.meta: // SLIDE 09 — FNA VS CORE NEEDLE BIOPSY

data.question: Which needle technique should be used?

branches.label: Fine-needle aspiration (22–25 gauge)
branches.detail: Cytology only — no architecture, rarely enough for molecular profiling. Cannot assess invasion through basement membranes.
branches.fix: Use for confirming known-primary mets or when architecture is not needed

branches.label: Core needle biopsy (14–18 gauge)
branches.detail: Preserves architecture — supports IHC and NGS. Required when invasion assessment determines diagnosis.
branches.fix: Use when diagnosis requires architecture or molecular profiling

resolver.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma — the extreme case
resolver.detail: Capsular invasion is required for diagnosis. FNA cannot establish invasion. The whole nodule must be excised — FNA cannot make this diagnosis at all.
